claims.text: The material family of interest is multiphase refractory high-entropy alloys, and the primary property is ductility under thermal aging.
A solutionized or as-cast BCC RHEA containing weak B2 ordering and minor compositional fluctuations has moderate ductility.
RHEAs with intermediate chemical ordering will undergo a ductile-brittle-ductile transition during aging.
Initial growth of B2 ordering during aging causes embrittlement.
Isothermal aging from 600–900 °C followed by aging above 1000 °C produces progressive ordering and then an order-disorder transition.
The degree of chemical short-range order and the volume fraction of B2 precipitates modulate the Peierls barrier and strain localization.
Low-temperature B2 ordering increases Peierls stress and promotes strain localization, leading to brittle fracture.
An order-disorder transition temperature of approximately 1120 K has been predicted for a related RHEA.
Above the order-disorder transition, ordered domains dissolve into a disordered BCC matrix.
Dissolution of ordered domains restores homogeneous plastic deformation and strain hardening, causing ductility recovery.
Ductility versus aging time or temperature will have a U- or V-shaped profile.
Solutionized Al0.5NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr in Condition 2 is largely single-phase BCC with weak B2 ordering and high ductility because its matrix is primarily disordered.
Fully ordered or phase-separated RHEAs have low ductility.
C14 Laves phase formation can deteriorate mechanical properties and increase cracking tendency.
The order-disorder transition is reached when SRO parameters tend toward zero.
If brittle Laves or Heusler phases form before the order-disorder transition, ductility recovery will not occur.
The exact order-disorder transition temperature of the proposed alloy has not been experimentally verified in the cited evidence.
Al0.5NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr is an appropriate weak-B2-ordering candidate for the aging experiment.
A monotonic decrease in ductility without recovery would falsify the proposed non-monotonic transition.
Ductility recovery while SRO remains high would falsify the claim that loss of ordering causes the recovery.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that formation of a brittle secondary phase before the ODTT is an anticipated condition under which recovery should not occur, whereas falsification rule (3) treats that same boundary-condition outcome as falsification of the hypothesis.
